question.worked_solution:
We perform the multiplication under a single radical and then simplify the result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{6{a}^{3}b}\cdot \sqrt{15abc} & = \\ \sqrt{6{a}^{3}b\cdot 15abc} & = \\ \sqrt{90{a}^{4}{b}^{2}c} & = \\ \sqrt{9{a}^{4}{b}^{2}\cdot 10c} & = \\ \sqrt{(3{a}^{2}b)^{2}\cdot 10c} & = \\ 3\cdot |{a}^{2}|\cdot |b|\cdot \sqrt{10c}\end{aligned}
$$

A squared number is always positive or zero, and the absolute value of any positive (or zero) number is itself, so we have that $|{a}^{2}|={a}^{2}$ and $|b|=b.$  Therefore, our final answer is

$$
\begin{aligned}3\cdot |{a}^{2}|\cdot |b|\cdot \sqrt{10c} & = \\ 3{a}^{2}b\sqrt{10c} & .\end{aligned}
$$
